data.narrative:
Hexana is a seed-stage nuclear energy company founded by Sylvain Nizou and Paul Gauthe that has raised €25M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 11 peers across nuclear energy—three public companies (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and eight private firms including Nano Nuclear Energy, Helion, Oklo, Valar Atomics, and X-Energy—though the narrow seed-stage cohort within this sector remains limited.

The stage-progression method is the primary applicable valuation framework. Using total capital raised (€25M) as a proxy for seed-stage value, a 2.5x step-up multiplier—typical for advancement from seed to Series A—yields an implied valuation of €62M. A peer-median approach was not actionable given insufficient comparables at Hexana's exact stage and valuation tier within nuclear energy; while six same-sector peers exist, none of the targeted filters produced the three or more datapoints necessary for robust median triangulation.

The analysis supports a valuation range of €53M to €72M, with a median point of €62M. This range reflects the 2.5x multiplier applied with ±15% sensitivity bounds. Key uncertainties center on the narrow peer set at the seed stage in nuclear energy and the reliance on a single methodological anchor. Investors should weight this valuation against facility-specific technical validation, regulatory pathway clarity, and capital intensity typical of the sector.
